body.heading: The rushed start
paragraphs: Many mornings begin at full speed: alarm, phone, headlines, messages, a small spike of urgency before your feet touch the floor. Your body takes the hint and stays braced for the rest of the day.
Five slower minutes will not fix a genuinely overloaded schedule, but they change the starting conditions. Beginning calm makes it easier to return to calm later.

body.heading: Design a gentler opening
paragraphs: Choose a tiny morning sequence and protect it: make the bed, drink a glass of water, look out of the window while the kettle boils, stretch while the shower warms up. Keep the phone out of the first five minutes if you can.
The exact contents matter less than the pace. Slow, ordinary actions done in order tell your nervous system that there is no emergency yet — and most mornings, there isn't one.

takeaway: Protect the first five minutes, and the day starts on your side.
